It sounds like you've been working hard to support your daughter, and it's understandable to feel concerned when these challenges persist. Some of what you're describing—difficulty with potty training, limited eye contact, and looking "through" people rather than at them—can be part of a range of developmental differences that are best understood through a professional evaluation.

I'd encourage you to talk with her pediatrician about what you're observing. They can refer you to a developmental specialist or early intervention program, which can provide a thorough assessment and, if needed, tailored strategies and therapies. Early support can make a meaningful difference, and you don't need to wait for things to resolve on their own before seeking guidance.

In the meantime, try to keep interactions low-pressure—forcing potty time when she's distressed may increase her anxiety around it. Follow her interests, celebrate small wins, and be gentle with yourselves too. You're clearly advocating for her, and that matters a lot.
